text: Code refactoring is the process of improving the structure of existing code without changing what it does. The main goal is to make code easier to read and understand. When programmers refactor, they clean up messy sections, remove duplication, and give variables clearer names. This helps reduce technical debt, which builds up over time when quick fixes are used instead of proper solutions. Refactoring does not add new features or fix bugs; the program should behave exactly the same after refactoring as it did before. Regular refactoring keeps a codebase healthy and makes future changes safer and faster.
